newsitem.title: USA: Haemonetics gets FDA okay on blood device.
newsitem.headline: Haemonetics gets FDA okay on blood device.

text.p: Haemonetics Corp said Tuesday the Food and Drug Administration has given it clearance to market automated blood collection devices that draws two pints of red cells from donors, doubling the amount currently collected.
The company said that the agency's premarketing clearance should help ease the chronic red blood cell shortages in the U.S. and abroad.
The approval follows by one year clearance for the same devices to be used by patients donating blood for their own surgical use.
Haemonetics said it was the sole company with FDA approval to market the devices.

John White, chairman, chief executive officer and president, said the automation afforded by the company's devices "is critical to our customers' ability to manage a shrinking donor population and limited blood supplies."
"We believe that red cell automation, over timne, will fundamentally change the way blood is collected in the U.S. and worldwide," he said.
